implemented: Additive SQLite and PostgreSQL migrations store user-scoped source references, revision, bounded reason codes and decisions without message plaintext.
Atomic recording preserves restored/dismissed decisions for the same revision; a changed revision is quarantined again.
Decisions require matching owner and revision. Inbox listing is user-scoped.

SpamInboxService derives authenticated ownership, verifies channel read permission or private/group membership, rejects self-message records and stale revisions, and rechecks source access for listed references.
Authenticated non-bot HTTP routes expose list, record, restore and dismiss with bounded JSON bodies. User-scoped keyset pagination uses a timestamp/source/message cursor; no plaintext is returned.

Account anonymization and hard-delete remove owned spam decisions; personal exports include only owned decision metadata. SQLite and PostgreSQL guards reject writes for deleted owners, with PostgreSQL retirement write-barrier integration.

Client Inbox exposes paginated spam references, source navigation, restore and dismiss. Failed decisions retain their rows and display errors. Unavailable references can be dismissed without source access, while restoration still requires source authorization.
Rendered channel/DM messages register local spam findings without sending plaintext. Inline restore records the source and commits a server restore decision before updating visibility.

Live channel/DM spam and loaded DM history register metadata in the background. Batches run at most four requests concurrently, request account affinity is checked, and failures show a retry action without discarding messages.

Loaded channel history and group history/search/live messages register local findings. Group message content and attachments are gated with reasons, restore and failed-registration retry controls. Group edits are classified again.

Committed spam decisions broadcast only to the owner's sessions. Connected clients apply account/source/revision-scoped restore decisions to message visibility, attention policy and displayed spam rows.

Ready/reconnect loads paginated owned restore/dismiss decisions. Snapshot merges preserve live decisions received after loading starts, reject stale-account responses and flag repeated cursors. Inbox refresh retries failed decision synchronization.

Database insert guards bound references to 5000 per owner while allowing retries/updates of existing keys; PostgreSQL serializes quota checks on the owner row. Metadata validation rejects malformed references, revision timestamps and duplicate/unknown reason codes.
OpenAPI documents spam inbox, decisions, restore and dismiss routes, access/revision semantics, metadata limits and quota failure.
Inbox conversation previews, channel/DM search result bodies, channel/DM reply previews and group reply excerpts apply reactive spam visibility before rendering content.

Saved-message bodies and composer reply previews use the same spam guard. ForwardMessageModal was inspected: it does not render source-message text or attachment previews; explicit forwarding behavior remains unchanged.
Spam inbox initial loading is explicit; refresh aborts outstanding paging and ignores old generation responses, preventing stale pages from contaminating a refreshed list.

Spam rows expose the existing explicit user-report dialog with spam preselected. Source content is not automatically loaded/shared; empty source plaintext has no content-sharing checkbox. Group reports currently use user context only.
